title: Protocols for endothelial cell isolation from mouse tissues: small intestine, colon, heart, and liver
protocol: Prepare small intestine digestion buffer right before isolation.
Add supplemented KnockOutTM DMEM-medium, 0.1% (w/v) collagenase I, 0.25% (w/v) collagenase IV, 0.25 U/mL Dispase, and 7.5 μg/mL DNAse I to the digestion buffer.
Prepare pre-digestion buffer right before isolation.
Add HBSS (Ca2+, Mg2+), 1.5 mM DTT, 5% (v/v) FBS, and 5 mM EDTA to the pre-digestion buffer.
Prepare cold HBSS (Ca2+, Mg2+).
Store small intestine digestion buffer and pre-digestion buffer at 4°C until needed.
Perform transcardial perfusion via left ventricle with ice-cold PBS at a rate of 2 mL/minute for 5 minutes.
Flush the fecal matter from the dissected small intestine with ice-cold HBSS using a syringe and elastic needle.
Open the small intestine longitudinally and cut it into very small pieces (4 mm²).
Place the pieces in a 50 mL conical tube (1 intestine per tube).
Add 25 mL of ice-cold pre-digestion buffer to the tube – invert 10-15 times.
Incubate with 37°C water bath for 20 minutes, shaking vigorously by hand every 5 minutes.
Vortex the content for 10 seconds after incubation.
Filter the content through a 100 μm cell strainer.
Collect undigested intestines from the strainer and place them in a new 50 mL conical tube containing 20 mL of pre-digestion buffer.
Incubate at 37°C water bath for another 20 minutes, shaking vigorously by hand every 5 minutes.
Vortex the content for 10 seconds after incubation.
Filter the content through a 100 μm cell strainer.
Collect undigested small intestines from the strainer.
Place collected intestines in gentleMACS C tubes containing pre-warmed digestion buffer at 37°C (3 mL per tube).
Close the tubes tightly and place them in the gentleMACS™ Octo Dissociator.
Run protocol 37C_m_LPDK_1 on the gentleMACS™ Octo Dissociator.
Stop enzymatic reaction by adding 5 mL of Wash Buffer 1 to each tube.
Filter cell suspension through a 100 μm cell strainer into a 50 mL conical tube.
Rinse the strainer with an additional 10 mL of Wash Buffer 1 and collect pass-through suspension in the same conical tube.
Centrifuge cells at 300 g for 10 min.
Carefully remove supernatant, noting its milky/cloudy appearance due to chyle content.
Resuspend pellet in 5 mL of Wash Buffer 1 and centrifuge again at 300 g for 5 min if necessary to clear supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in an appropriate amount of Wash Buffer 1.
Add the appropriate volume of CD31 MicroBeads to the cell suspension according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Mix thoroughly and incubate for 15 min at 4°C.
Wash cells by adding 3 mL of Wash Buffer 1.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Prepare collection tubes and LS columns according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Place the column in the suitable magnetic separator.
Rinse the column with 3 mL of Wash Buffer.
Remove the supernatant from the cells.
Resuspend the pellet in 0.5 mL of Wash Buffer 1.
Apply the cell suspension onto the LS column through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Wash the LS column 3 times with 3 mL Wash Buffer 1.
Pipette 5 mL Wash Buffer 1 onto the LS column.
Flush out the fraction containing the magnetically labeled cells by firmly applying the plunger supplied with the column.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 g for 5 min, remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 0.5 mL Wash Buffer 1-based staining solution containing CD31-FITC (1:300), CD45-PE-Cyanine7 (1:700), and eFluor 450 (1:1000).
Stain the cells for 30 min at 4°C in the dark.
Add 3 mL of Wash Buffer 1 and centrifuge the stained cells at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C, remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in Wash Buffer 1 (between 200 μL and 0.5 mL) based on the pellet size and proceed with FACS.
Sort viable, CD45-, CD31+ cells to collection tubes.
Sort ECs to collection medium (10% v/v FBS in PBS) in an Eppendorf (∼ 200 μL) or 15 mL conical tube (∼ 2 mL).
Prepare colon digestion buffer right before isolation containing supplemented KnockOutTM DMEM-medium, 0.1% (w/v) collagenase I, 0.25% (w/v) collagenase IV, 0.625 U/mL Dispase, and 7.5 μg/mL DNAse I.
Prepare PBS-based Wash Buffer 2 containing 3% (v/v) FBS in PBS and 10 mM EDTA.
Store the freshly prepared colon digestion buffer and Wash Buffer 2 at 4°C until needed.
Perform transcardial perfusion via the left ventricle with ice-cold PBS at a rate of 2 mL/minute for 5 minutes.
Dissect the colon and flush fecal matter using a 20 mL syringe and an elastic needle with ice-cold PBS.
Open the colon longitudinally and fix it at both ends if necessary.
Swiftly scrape out the mucus from the inner surface of the colon using a sterile scalpel blade.
Cut the colon into very small pieces that can pass through a cut P1000 tip (approximately 0.8 mm).
Transfer the colon pieces to a 50 mL conical tube containing 10 mL of colon digestion buffer.
Rinse the Petri dish with an additional 4 mL of colon digestion buffer and transfer the cell suspension to a gentleMACS C tube using a P1000 micropipette.
Incubate the cell suspension in the gentle MACS C tube for 15 minutes at 37°C.
Shake the tube vigorously by hand every 5 minutes to ensure rapid tissue dissociation.
Run m_lung_01 protocol.
Stop enzymatic reaction by adding 15 mL of Wash Buffer 2.
Filter content using a 100 μm cell strainer into a 50 mL conical tube.
Divide filtered cells over two 15 mL conical tubes.
Centrifuge both cell suspensions at 300 g for 7 minutes.
Remove supernatant and resuspend pellets in 5 mL of Wash Buffer 2.
Pool previously divided samples.
Filter content using a 40 μm cell strainer into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Transfer content to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 300 g for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant and wash pellet with 5 mL Wash Buffer 2.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 300 g for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in an appropriate amount of Wash Buffer 1.
Add the appropriate volume of CD31 MicroBeads to the suspension according to manufacturer's instructions.
Resuspend cells in 90 μL of Wash Buffer 1.
Determine the cell number.
Mix resuspended cells with CD31 MicroBeads (10 μL for up to 1 × 10^7 total cells) and incubate at 4°C for 15 minutes.
Wash cells by adding 3 mL of Wash Buffer 2 and centrifuge at 300 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 0.5 mL of Wash Buffer 2.
Apply the cell suspension onto the prepared LS column through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Wash the LS column 3 times with 3 mL Wash Buffer 2, adding buffer each time once the column reservoir is empty.
Pipette 5 mL Wash Buffer 1 onto the LS column.
Flush out the fraction containing magnetically labeled cells (CD31-positive fraction) by firmly applying the plunger supplied with the column.
Prepare unstained cell control for flow cytometry analysis.
Prepare viability control for flow cytometry analysis.
Prepare Fluorescence Minus One (FMO) control for flow cytometry analysis.
Optionally, prepare isotype controls for flow cytometry analysis.
Prepare compensation controls using compensation beads for each fluorophore.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 0.5 mL Wash Buffer 1-based staining solution containing CD31 (PECAM-1) Monoclonal Antibody, CD45 Monoclonal Antibody, and Viability Dye.
Stain the cells for 30 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Add 3 mL of Wash Buffer 1.
Centrifuge the stained cells at 300 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in Wash Buffer 1 (between 200 μL and 0.5 mL based on the pellet size).
Proceed with FACS.
Sort viable, CD45-, CD31+ cells to collection tubes.
Sort the ECs to collection medium (10% (v/v) FBS in PBS).
Perform transcardial perfusion via the left ventricle with ice-cold PBS at a rate of 2 mL/minute for 5 minutes.
Harvest the hearts and cut them into small pieces (approximately 2 mm²).
Pool all heart pieces in a 50 ml conical tube containing 5 ml of heart digestion buffer.
Incubate the sample in digestion buffer in a 37°C water bath for 25 minutes, shaking vigorously by hand every 5-10 minutes.
Place tubes in gentleMACS™ Dissociator.
Run protocol C as pre-programmed by manufacturer.
Pipette the cell suspension up and down using serological pipets with decreasing tip sizes (25 mL > 5 mL > 10 mL).
Stop enzymatic reaction by adding 25 mL of Wash Buffer 1.
Filter cell suspension through a 100 μm cell strainer.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 g for 7 minutes.
Collect supernatant into a new 50 mL conical tube and centrifuge again at 300 g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 5 mL of Wash Buffer 1 and filter through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Wash conical tube and filter with an additional 4 mL of Wash Buffer 1.
Resuspend pellet in 4 mL of Wash Buffer 1 and filter the cell suspension through the 40 μm cell strainer used previously.
Pool both fractions and transfer to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 minutes, remove the supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in an appropriate amount of Wash Buffer 1.
Add the appropriate volume of CD31 MicroBeads according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Resuspend cells in 90 μL of Wash Buffer 1.
Determine the number of cells.
For up to 1 × 10^7 total cells, add 10 μL of CD31 MicroBeads to the cell suspension.
Mix and incubate for 15 min at 4°C.
Wash the cells by adding 3 mL of Wash Buffer 1.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 0.5 mL of Wash Buffer 1.
Prepare collection tubes and LS columns according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Place the column in a suitable magnetic separator.
Rinse the column with 3 mL of Wash Buffer.
Apply the cell suspension onto the prepared LS column through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Wash the LS column 3 times with 3 mL of Wash Buffer 1.
Add buffer to the column once the reservoir is empty after each wash.
Remove the LS column from the separator and place it onto a new 15 mL conical collection tube.
Pipette 5 mL of Wash Buffer 1 onto the LS column.
Firmly apply the plunger supplied with the column to flush out the fraction containing the magnetically labeled cells.
Prepare unstained cell (US) control for flow cytometry analysis beforehand.
Prepare viability control (VB) for flow cytometry analysis beforehand.
Prepare Fluorescence Minus One (FMO) control for flow cytometry analysis beforehand.
Optionally prepare isotype controls for flow cytometry analysis beforehand.
Prepare compensation controls for each fluorophore using compensation beads, such as OneComp eBeads™ Compensation Beads from Thermo Fisher Scientific.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet in 0.5 mL of Wash Buffer 1-based staining solution.
Stain the cells for 30 min at 4°C in the dark.
Add 3 mL of Wash Buffer 1 and centrifuge the stained cells at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C, remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in Wash Buffer 1 based on the pellet size between 200 μL and 0.5 mL.
Proceed with FACS to sort viable, CD45-, CD31+ cells to collection tubes.
Sort ECs to collection medium (10% (v/v) FBS in PBS) in an Eppendorf (∼ 200 μL) or 15 mL conical tube (∼ 2 mL).
Prepare liver digestion buffer containing supplemented KnockOutTM DMEM-medium, 0.1% collagenase I, 0.1% collagenase II, 0.25 U/mL Dispase, and 7.5 μg/mL DNAse I.
Store the freshly prepared liver digestion buffer at 4°C until needed.
Perform transcardial perfusion via the left ventricle with ice-cold PBS followed by additional perfusion with liver digestion buffer for 5 min at a rate of 2 mL/minute.
Transfer a single murine liver into a 50 ml conical tube containing 5 ml of liver digestion buffer.
Incubate the sample in a 37°C water bath for 30 min, shaking vigorously by hand every 10 min.
Mix the sample by pipetting up and down using a 10 ml serological pipette.
Stop the digestion by adding 8 ml of wash buffer to the tube.
Mix the cell suspension thoroughly.
Filter the cell suspension through a 100 μm cell strainer.
Centrifuge the filtered cell suspension at 300 g for 7 min.
Remove the supernatant carefully with a pipette.
Repeat washing step by adding 5 mL of Wash Buffer 1.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 300 g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the pellet in an appropriate amount of Wash Buffer 1.
Add the appropriate volume of CD31 MicroBeads to the suspension according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Mix well and incubate for 20 min at 4°C.
Wash cells by adding 3 mL of Wash Buffer 1.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Prepare collection tubes and LS columns according to manufacturer's instructions.
Place the column in a suitable magnetic separator.
Rinse the column with 3 mL of Wash Buffer.
Remove supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 0.5 mL of Wash Buffer 1.
Apply the cell suspension onto the prepared LS column through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Wash the LS column 3 times with 3 mL Wash Buffer 1, adding buffer each time once the reservoir is empty.
Remove the LS column from the separator and place it onto a new 15 mL conical collection tube.
Pipette 5 mL Wash Buffer 1 onto the LS column.
Firmly apply the plunger to flush out the fraction containing magnetically labeled cells.
Prepare all required controls for flow cytometry analysis beforehand.
Create an unstained cell (US) control.
Establish a viability control (VB).
Generate Fluorescence Minus One (FMO) control.
Optionally prepare isotype controls.
Set up compensation controls for each fluorophore using compensation beads.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 0.5 mL Wash Buffer 1-based staining solution containing CD11b-PE, CD31-FITC, CD45-PE-Cyanine7, and eFluor 450.
Stain the cells for 30 min at 4°C in the dark.
Add 3 mL of Wash Buffer 1 to the stained cells.
Centrifuge the stained cells at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in Wash Buffer 1 based on the pellet size between 200 μL and 0.5 mL.
Proceed with FACS to sort viable, CD11b-, and CD31+ cells to collection tubes.
Sort the ECs to collection medium (10% v/v FBS in PBS) in an Eppendorf (∼ 200 μL) or 15 mL conical tube (∼ 2 mL).
